title: Staying close to Johnny St. Cyr; his cataract and guitar
summary: He had no formal lessons but stayed beside Johnny St. Cyr at the Tulane gym dances, and they are still friends. They discuss St. Cyr's wife's death, his cataract operation and the guitar he plans to send the museum.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up a first guitar or banjo, self-taught

blocks.x: Did you ever have any more lessons there during that period?

No, no. Outside of, well, up at the Tulane Gym when I began hearing the real good bands, I would stick on Johnny St. Cyr's neck a whole evening. I never left him, and he would always show me little things to do. There's no formal lessons there. No. Incidentally, we're still friends, Bill. I get a letter from him at least once a month. He wired me and wrote me when his wife died recently, and he's just had a cataract operation. He said he had that.
I didn't know he had that.
Some friends said, well, you're going to have it too late, maybe not save it.

Well, the last news I got was about two weeks ago from a fellow by the name of, that was in here recently. Slingsby. Slingsby, who wrote me, I have a letter from him just the other day, saying that Johnny was going into the hospital. I haven't heard how it came out.
He's going to put it off and...

Now, he's going to send us his guitar for the museum. He's promised me that, but he won't send it because it's broken. I said, I don't give a damn. Send it. I'll fix it. I'll get Bill to fix it for me.
I'll get it. So, anyway, when we began...
